existing_capabilities: Fingerprint via /-/healthy body match + /api/v1/status/buildinfo JSON parse (version extracted)
HTTP + HTTPS fallback via unverified SSL context
GET /api/v1/status/config — sets config_readable, coarse count of '- targets:' / 'static_configs:' blocks (scrape_targets_hint)
GET /api/v1/query?query=up — sets query_open (only the literal `up` query)
POST /-/reload — sets admin_writable (mis-attributed to --web.enable-admin-api; see gaps)
svcprobe.iter_probe budget/progress integration; analyze() returns targets/findings/runbooks/probes/stats

missing_capabilities.name: GET /federate?match[]={__name__=~".+"} — federation bulk exfil
missing_capabilities.description: Prometheus federation endpoint returns the current value of every matched series in one shot; permissive matcher dumps the entire live TSDB view (labels + values). Frequently left open even when /api/v1/query is fronted by auth. Not touched today. Largest metric-data exfil primitive.

missing_capabilities.name: GET /debug/pprof/cmdline (+ goroutine, heap, profile)
missing_capabilities.description: net/http/pprof is registered by default in Prometheus's promhttp mux. /debug/pprof/cmdline leaks full process argv — including --web.config.file, --storage.tsdb.path, and any secret passed via CLI flag. goroutine dump leaks internal state / upstreams. Not probed.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: net/http/pprof (pkg.go.dev/net/http/pprof); Prometheus exposes pprof on the web listener

missing_capabilities.name: POST /api/v1/admin/tsdb/delete_series?match[]=... — data destruction
missing_capabilities.description: True --web.enable-admin-api endpoint. Deletes series matching match[] — erases evidence around a time window. Module misses it entirely and mis-attributes /-/reload to --web.enable-admin-api.

missing_capabilities.name: POST /api/v1/admin/tsdb/snapshot + clean_tombstones
missing_capabilities.description: Snapshot forces full TSDB snapshot under --storage.tsdb.path; repeat calls fill disk (DoS) and produce on-disk artifacts an attacker with FS read can grab. clean_tombstones removes prior delete-series records so audit trail vanishes.

missing_capabilities.name: POST /-/quit — lifecycle DoS
missing_capabilities.description: Graceful shutdown endpoint. Gated by --web.enable-lifecycle (same flag as /-/reload, NOT --web.enable-admin-api as the current finding text says). If /-/reload accepts POST, /-/quit almost certainly does — full monitoring blackout on demand.

missing_capabilities.name: Finding-text bug: /-/reload attributed to --web.enable-admin-api
missing_capabilities.description: prom_admin_writable finding + module docstring claim /-/reload maps to --web.enable-admin-api. Wrong flag: /-/reload and /-/quit are gated by --web.enable-lifecycle; /api/v1/admin/tsdb/* is what --web.enable-admin-api gates. Remediation will misdirect defenders.

missing_capabilities.name: GET /api/v1/targets — full scrape topology without config
missing_capabilities.description: Returns every active/dropped scrape target with discovered labels, health, lastError, lastScrape. Frequently reachable even when /api/v1/status/config is blocked. Yields resolved IPs from SD (not just static hostnames); lastError often quotes internal URLs and TLS chain fragments.

missing_capabilities.name: GET /api/v1/status/flags + /api/v1/status/runtimeinfo
missing_capabilities.description: flags returns every runtime flag value (config file path, TSDB path, retention, web listen addr); runtimeinfo returns CWD, hostname, GOMAXPROCS, chunk counts, storage retention. Not probed.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Prometheus HTTP API — 'Runtime Information' and 'Flag Values'

missing_capabilities.name: GET /api/v1/rules + /api/v1/alerts + /api/v1/alertmanagers
missing_capabilities.description: rules dumps recording+alerting rule bodies (thresholds reveal detection logic — stay under). alerts lists firing alerts (known-broken services = soft targets). alertmanagers returns every Alertmanager URL Prometheus pages — a direct pivot list.

missing_capabilities.name: GET /api/v1/labels + /api/v1/label/{name}/values + /api/v1/series
missing_capabilities.description: Label enumeration returns every job/instance/namespace/cluster/pod known to the TSDB — internal architecture map even when `up` is blocked. /api/v1/series matches series without querying values (sometimes ACL'd separately from /query).
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Prometheus HTTP API — 'Getting label names', 'Querying label values', 'Finding series by label matchers'

missing_capabilities.name: Host/OS fingerprint queries beyond `up`
missing_capabilities.description: When query_open, only `up` is queried. High-value queries not attempted: node_uname_info (kernel + hostname), node_dmi_info (BIOS vendor / product = cloud vs bare-metal), node_boot_time_seconds (uptime => patch level), node_filesystem_size_bytes (disk layout), process_start_time_seconds (per-service uptime), kube_pod_info / kube_node_info (k8s inventory), cloudwatch_*/aws_*/azure_* (cloud metadata). Passive fingerprint battery worth harvesting.

missing_capabilities.name: Config-parse depth: extract embedded creds + SD backends
missing_capabilities.description: When config_readable, module only counts target blocks. Not extracted: bearer_token, bearer_token_file, basic_auth.password/password_file, authorization.credentials, tls_config.key_file, remote_write[].url+authorization, remote_read[].url, kubernetes_sd_configs (api_server + role + tls), consul_sd_configs (server + token), ec2/gce/azure/scaleway/digitalocean_sd (cloud IAM creds), oauth2.client_secret. Each is a movable secret and every SD backend URL is a new pivot host.

missing_capabilities.name: GET /metrics — Prometheus self-scrape endpoint
missing_capabilities.description: Prometheus exposes its own metrics on /metrics (self-scrape). Leaks prometheus_build_info (exact revision/branch/goversion, not just version), prometheus_config_last_reload_success_timestamp, prometheus_engine_query_duration_seconds (evidence of admin activity), prometheus_target_sync_length_seconds by scrape_job (job names). Often ungated even when /api/v1/* is proxied.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Prometheus instrumentation — /metrics on the same port

missing_capabilities.name: Push Gateway probe (9091 detected but not exercised)
missing_capabilities.description: is_prometheus() matches 9091/9092 but probe() only speaks Prometheus server API. Push Gateway on 9091: GET / lists all pushed job/instance groups; PUT/POST /metrics/job/<job>[/instance/<i>] accepts arbitrary metrics from anyone — inject fake up=1 for missing hosts (hide takedowns), invert SLO metrics (drown SOC). DELETE /metrics/job/<job> wipes existing groups.

missing_capabilities.name: Auth-enforced state detection + credentialed trial
missing_capabilities.description: When endpoints return 401/403 the probe treats them as 'not open' and emits nothing. Should distinguish 'auth enforced' from 'endpoint absent'. Prometheus native web.config.file supports basic_auth_users since 2.24 and mTLS. analyze() takes creds but nothing consumes them — no Authorization: Basic trial, no bearer_token trial, no reuse of tokens harvested from sibling modules (Consul, k8s, Grafana).

missing_capabilities.name: TLS server_config disclosure via /api/v1/status/config
missing_capabilities.description: When yaml is returned, tls_server_config fields (cert_file, key_file paths, client_ca_file, min_version) not extracted. Paths hint at PKI layout; client_ca_file is a direct pivot to the internal CA if FS becomes reachable.

missing_capabilities.name: Body cap of 200_000 bytes drops large configs / federate output silently
missing_capabilities.description: Real prometheus.yml with k8s + many rule_files easily exceeds 200KB; /federate output is many MB. resp.read(200_000) truncates without a marker, then json.loads fails silently in except — config_readable stays False on the very deployments that leak the most. Chunk-read with a much larger cap on config/federate, or at minimum record 'truncated'.

missing_capabilities.name: CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * not checked
missing_capabilities.description: Prometheus supports --web.cors.origin which is commonly misconfigured to `.*`. Any authenticated user's browser can then be forced to query the API from an attacker page (drive-by exfil). Header not inspected.

missing_capabilities.name: Version-to-CVE mapping absent
missing_capabilities.description: version is captured but never checked against Prometheus CVEs — e.g. CVE-2019-3826 (federate SSRF, <2.7.1), CVE-2023-2569 (resource consumption /api/v1/labels), CVE-2024-1394 (memory leak /api/v1/query). No CVE bucket emitted for downstream reporting.

missing_capabilities.name: Remote-write reload-abuse SSRF/exfil chain
missing_capabilities.description: admin_writable + config_readable together = attacker POSTs modified prometheus.yml (via any writable path referenced from it) and hits /-/reload to point remote_write at attacker URL. All metrics stream out over authenticated remote_write. Prose mentions exfil, but no chain finding is emitted for the attack-path graph.

missing_capabilities.name: PromQL DoS not surfaced when query_open
missing_capabilities.description: Open /api/v1/query permits expensive PromQL — e.g. `topk(1e6, {__name__=~".+"}[30d])`, unbounded range queries — which OOM or wedge the process. Distinct medium/high finding separate from the info-disc angle.

priority_gaps: P0: /federate bulk-exfil probe + finding (largest missing attack primitive)
P0: Config-parse depth — lift bearer_token, basic_auth, remote_write.authorization, kubernetes_sd api_server, consul_sd token, ec2/gce/azure SD creds; feed cred store + pivot list
P1: /api/v1/targets — network map without needing config read
P1: /-/quit lifecycle DoS + fix /-/reload lifecycle-vs-admin-api attribution
P1: Push Gateway (9091) — GET / and PUT /metrics/job/* metric-injection
P1: Auth-enforced state (401/403) as distinct outcome + credentialed trial via creds arg + harvested bearer tokens
P2: Passive host-fingerprint query battery (node_uname_info, node_dmi_info, kube_node_info, process_start_time_seconds) when query_open
P2: /api/v1/labels + label-values + /series for topology when /query is blocked
P2: /metrics self-scrape endpoint (build_info revision, job names, config-reload timestamps)
P2: 200KB body cap truncates real configs / federate silently — chunk-read + truncated flag
P2: Chain finding: admin_writable + config_readable → remote_write exfil / rule-file SSRF
P3: Version-to-CVE mapping for buildinfo.version (CVE-2019-3826 etc.)
P3: Query-DoS finding companion to query_open (expensive PromQL)
cross_service_wire_gaps: Bearer tokens + basic_auth creds parsed from prometheus.yml → cred store (currently only counted). Consumers: HTTP-auth trial, Kubernetes API, Grafana, Consul, Vault modules.
kubernetes_sd_configs.api_server URL + role + tls → Kubernetes service module as a new target (with its own creds).
consul_sd_configs.server + token → Consul service module target + Consul ACL token cred.
ec2_sd / gce_sd / azure_sd blocks → cloud-metadata / IAM cred store; consumed by other cloud modules.
remote_write[].url + authorization.credentials → Grafana Cloud / Cortex / Thanos / Mimir endpoint list; downstream observability-backend probe + bearer-cred entry.
/api/v1/alertmanagers → Alertmanager (9093) service module targets (exact URLs, not just hosts).
/api/v1/targets discovered scrape targets → host inventory as newly-observed IP:port with role-labels (node_exporter@9100, cadvisor@8080, blackbox_exporter@9115). Backfill Host/Port records.
blackbox_exporter targets discovered → SSRF-pivot candidate list (blackbox /probe is a classic SSRF gadget).
node_exporter targets discovered → node-exporter service module seed (no dedicated module today, but the target list is the seed).
Config paths from /api/v1/status/flags (--config.file, --storage.tsdb.path, --web.config.file) → filesystem-read post-exploitation module (what to grep for once shell is obtained).
prom_admin_writable + prom_config_readable together → attack-path graph edge 'metric-exfil-via-remote_write-swap' the exploit orchestrator should synthesize.
Push Gateway writable → alert/SOC-poisoning primitive for the exploit orchestrator (no path there today).
summary: Recce's prometheus module covers the four most-cited public-web attack surfaces (config read, query open, admin reload, buildinfo fingerprint) but misses the higher-value ones on the same daemon: /federate bulk exfil, /debug/pprof/cmdline argv leak, and the actual --web.enable-admin-api endpoints under /api/v1/admin/tsdb/* (delete_series, snapshot, clean_tombstones). Config parsing stops at target counts — the embedded bearer tokens, basic_auth, remote_write.authorization, and *_sd_configs cloud/consul/k8s creds that make Prometheus a credential goldmine are never lifted for the cred store or downstream modules. /-/reload is mis-attributed to --web.enable-admin-api (correct flag is --web.enable-lifecycle) which will misdirect remediation. Passive endpoints /api/v1/targets, /status/flags, /status/runtimeinfo, /rules, /alerts, /alertmanagers, /labels, and /metrics all leak topology and are not requested. Push Gateway (9091) is recognized by is_prometheus() but never probed — its unauth /metrics/job/* PUT is a distinct metric-injection primitive that poisons SOC alerts. Auth-enforced (401/403) is silently treated as 'closed' with no credentialed trial, and the analyze() creds arg is unused. Implementation caveat: 200KB body cap drops real configs and /federate output silently.
notes: Fix required alongside gaps: docstring + prom_admin_writable finding attribute /-/reload to --web.enable-admin-api; correct flag is --web.enable-lifecycle. The real --web.enable-admin-api surface (/api/v1/admin/tsdb/*) is not probed. resp.read(200_000) truncates real configs and any /federate response, so the highest-value bodies are the ones most likely to be silently dropped. Tests only exercise happy-path + 403; no 401/auth-enforced case, no truncation case, no push-gateway case, no federation case — expanding coverage should follow module additions.
